beats.subline: Wednesday, September 23, 2026 close — stocks fell broadly as the 10-year Treasury yield jumped to its highest level since 2007.
beats.body: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 5.1%, a 19-year high, after stronger-than-expected business-activity data raised the odds of another Fed rate hike; rate-sensitive tech names led the Nasdaq's decline as markets also looked ahead to Thursday's Trump-Xi summit in Washington.

beats.headline: Zelenskyy urges Trump to arrange trilateral summit with Putin as Russian strikes kill six hours after their call
beats.body: Hours after speaking with Trump, Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said the two should move 'as quickly as possible' toward a trilateral meeting with Putin and proposed a ceasefire on energy-infrastructure strikes; Russian drone and missile attacks on Kyiv and Donetsk killed six people that same day, underscoring the gap between the diplomatic push and events on the ground.

beats.headline: Xi Jinping arrives at White House for high-stakes summit on trade, Taiwan, AI and the Iran war
beats.body: Xi's visit -- his first to Washington in over a decade -- includes a Rose Garden military review, a bilateral meeting and a state dinner Thursday; Beijing wants Trump to permanently halt the paused $14 billion Taiwan arms package and ease chip export curbs, while Taipei says it remains confident US arms sales will continue regardless of the summit's outcome.

beats.headline: USS Abraham Lincoln nears record deployment length as Navy blockade operations continue off Iran
beats.body: The carrier strike group made a brief Guam stop after 307 days deployed and is now steaming toward San Diego, approaching the USS Gerald R. Ford's deployment-length record, while USS George H.W. Bush continues Arabian Sea blockade operations nearly six months in, having redirected more than 110 commercial vessels for compliance as of September 21.

beats.headline: Pentagon's GenAI.mil platform grows to 1.7 million users as officials plan to push AI into classified networks
beats.body: Speaking at the DefenseTalks conference, Pentagon AI officials said roughly 500,000 of the platform's 1.7 million users are now daily 'power users' who have built 100,000 task-specific AI agents, and that frontier models will be extended beyond the unclassified network onto SIPR, JWICS and Special Access Programs.

beats.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Marketplace, letting enterprise customers buy partner AI tools with committed spend
beats.body: The new marketplace centralizes more than 2,000 plugins and connectors, Claude-powered products from partners like CrowdStrike and Snowflake, and consulting services from firms including Accenture and Deloitte, letting customers apply their committed Anthropic spend toward third-party purchases.

beats.headline: Bears QB picture muddles further as Tyson Bagent enters concussion protocol ahead of Eagles game
beats.body: With Caleb Williams still week-to-week on a hamstring injury and Bagent now in the concussion protocol after relieving him Sunday, 38-year-old Case Keenum practiced Wednesday and is the likely starter for Monday night's home game against Philadelphia; coach Ben Johnson said the decision won't be final until later in the week and the team isn't planning to add another quarterback.

beats.headline: Byron's No. 24 rolls out its RAPTOR paint scheme for this weekend's Kansas Chase race
beats.body: Hendrick Motorsports previewed its paint schemes for Sunday's Kansas Speedway race, with Byron's charcoal-and-green RAPTOR livery -- now a primary scheme for the full 2026 season rather than a one-off -- set to run at the first mile-and-a-half track of the Round of 12.

beats.headline: PCA sets 2027 General Assembly for Milwaukee, first Upper Midwest gathering since 1987
beats.body: The host committee announced the 2027 General Assembly theme 'Come and See,' to be held June 14-18 at Milwaukee's Baird Center, hosted jointly by the Wisconsin, Chicago Metro, Korean Central and Northern Illinois presbyteries -- only the 11th Assembly held outside the Southeast.
